title: Handling of the inspection report on the Stanislas private school
description: An inspection report by the IGESR on the Paris private Catholic school Stanislas, commissioned under Attal's predecessor Pap Ndiaye, was sent to Attal as Education Minister on 2 August 2023 and became public when Mediapart revealed it in January 2024. It recorded that the law on the weekly catechism hour was not applied and that boys and girls were separated during relationship and sex education sessions. Attal is not the principal subject of the affair, which centred on his successor Amélie Oudéa-Castéra, whose children attended the school, and on the inspectorate itself; according to Oudéa-Castéra, Attal followed the report with an action plan of about fifteen measures entrusted to the regional education authority and the inspectorate, and a question to the government records that he initiated action when the report was sent. In April 2025 a parliamentary inquiry heard that the report's conclusions had been altered to protect the school, with an expurgated version sent to Attal and his chief of staff in August 2023 without all the inspectors general being informed — allegations directed at the inspectorate rather than at Attal.
key_facts: 2 August 2023: the IGESR report on Stanislas was sent to Attal as Education Minister
The report found the weekly catechism hour law unapplied and girls and boys separated in sex education sessions
Attal responded with an action plan of about fifteen measures, according to Amélie Oudéa-Castéra
April 2025: a parliamentary inquiry heard that the conclusions had been altered before transmission, without all inspectors general being informed
